title: Net Effective Rent: A Clear Commercial Lease Guide
excerpt: Net effective rent can help compare incentives, but it must be calculated consistently and considered with the full occupancy cost.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Net Effective Rent Explained | Your Office Space
metaDescription: Understand net effective rent, its assumptions and its role in comparing commercial lease proposals.
body:
Net effective rent is a comparison measure that adjusts rent for a quantified incentive over a defined period. It can be useful, but only when every proposal uses the same method.

## Start with the inputs

Record the rent basis, area, term, review assumptions, incentive value and timing. State whether figures include or exclude tax and outgoings.

## Keep the method consistent

Apply the same time period and calculation approach to each option. If assumptions differ, show them rather than forcing a misleading comparison.

## Do not confuse one metric with total cost

Net effective rent may not include outgoings, parking, utilities, fitout, relocation, finance costs or make-good. Build a separate total occupancy cost model.

## Test the form of the incentive

Rent-free periods, abatements and fitout contributions can affect timing, cash flow and risk differently. Check the legal documents and conditions with appropriate advisers.

## Keep an audit trail

Store the source proposal, calculation date, assumptions and reviewer. Update the model when commercial terms change.

Your Office Space can help structure a consistent comparison of shortlisted lease proposals.
